stops.note: to live, combined with super- (over, beyond)
to live beyond, to outlive, from super- (beyond) and vivere (to live)
carried into French for continuing to live after an event
stops.meaning: to continue to live after an event

stops.note: settled as the English word for continuing to live despite hardship or danger
stops.meaning: to continue to live despite hardship or danger

current_meaning: to continue living or existing despite hardship, danger, or difficulty
